text: You checked on the kiln from the inside.
You lived to a great age, which in this era was thirty-one. They buried you with a pot, in case you got thirsty.
You died at a great age, still arguing about lids.
You died rich in pots, which nobody else was allowed to make.
The swollen jar went off while you were leaning over it, which was brave and brief.
notes: Named by the sealing answers (prov-swollen, prov-cb-lid)

text: The far side of the hills had bears. The bears had never tasted preserved food, or you.
notes: Named by "Go with them" in prov-after-travel

text: You kept the smoking fire going for three days straight. On the fourth, it kept you.
You tasted one experiment too many. It tasted you back.
You boiled the sea for another month, to be sure. The sea was fine. You were not.
notes: Named by "Boil seawater yourself" in prov-salt

text: The goose won the rematch. It still guards your jar, and now your grave.
notes: Named by "Negotiate with the goose" in prov-goose

text: You were flattened in the rush for the last jar. The neighbours sent flowers, and a bag.
notes: Named by "Share the stores" in prov-after-share

text: You were counting the top shelf when the top shelf came down to be counted.
notes: Named by "Count them yourself" in prov-after-count

text: You won your winter against the Naysayer, then challenged the next one on your own. It won.
notes: Named by "Challenge him to a winter" in prov-after-naysayer

text: You lived a long life and never once went hungry, which in your family was a first.
You lived a long life, eating everything the day you got it. Your funeral feast was eaten at a sprint.
notes: A life that left a failed design: the food still rots

text: You died in winter, well fed, while the elder counted the jars at your funeral.
You died at a great age, in your own house, beside a full larder. The neighbours got there first.
